source_text: Venimus igitur ad propositum. Hoc enim dirigebamus et hoc praestruebamus allocutionis praefatione, ut iam hinc de eo congrediamur de quo adversarii provocant. Scripturas obtendunt, et hac sua audacia statim quosdam movent. In ipso vero congressu firmos quidem fatigant, infirmos capiunt, medios cum scrupulo dimittunt. Hunc igitur potissimum gradum obstruimus non admittendi eos ad ullam de scripturis disputationem. Si hae sunt illae vires eorum, uti eas habere possint, dispici debet, cui competat possessio scripturarum, ne is admittatur ad eas cui nullo modo competit.
thought_title: Heretics must be barred from arguing over the Scriptures
orientation: Tertullian is now moving to the main point of his treatise: heretics use the Scriptures to argue, but they must not be allowed to do so because the Scriptures do not belong to them.
pass_a_gloss: We have come therefore to the purpose. For we were directing toward this and we were building this up beforehand by the preface of the address, so that from here on we may engage about that about which the adversaries challenge. They put forward the Scriptures, and by this boldness of theirs they immediately disturb certain people. In the actual encounter, however, they weary the strong indeed, they capture the weak, they send away those in the middle with scruple. Therefore we block this step especially, of not admitting them to any dispute about the Scriptures. If these are those strengths of theirs, so that they may be able to have them, it must be examined to whom the possession of the Scriptures belongs, lest that person be admitted to them to whom it in no way belongs.

choices.why: Keeps the legal-rhetorical sense of the main point of the argument, matching the treatise's forensic framing.
Preserves the architectural metaphor of laying groundwork, which fits Tertullian's methodical argument.
Captures the defensive, screen-like use of Scripture by heretics, as if holding it up as a shield.
Keeps the Latin noun for a lingering doubt or unease, which is more precise than a general word for doubt.
Preserves the spatial metaphor of blocking a path or entrance, which matches the legal objection theme.
Renders the legal sense of rightful ownership or jurisdiction, central to the praescriptio argument.

pass_b_english: So we have come to the purpose. This is what we were directing our course toward, and what we were building up beforehand with the preface of our address: that from this point we may engage the matter on which our adversaries challenge us. They put forward the Scriptures, and by this boldness of theirs they immediately disturb some people. In the actual encounter, they weary the strong, capture the weak, and send away those in between with lingering unease. This step, then, above all, we block: they are not to be admitted to any dispute over the Scriptures. If these are their strength, so that they may possess them, it must be examined to whom the possession of the Scriptures belongs, so that no one may be admitted to them to whom it in no way belongs.
